A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AlphaEdit, with matching core equations, experiments and substantial shared text. Both versions, including their figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original sequential-editing experiments on three language models, general-capability evaluations, representation analyses and appendix case studies.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds comparator, model, benchmark, data-size sensitivity and runtime results in Appendices C.5–C.9.

M1.justification: The null-space projection, regularized objectives and closed-form update in Equations 8–15 remain unchanged. Appendix C.7 adds a limited procedural adaptation for KnowEdit: automatically excluding examples with unusually high hidden-state norms during sequential editing to avoid instability.

E1.justification: V3 adds evaluations on KnowEdit's wiki_recent and wikibio subsets, LEME long-form generation and MQuAKE multi-hop reasoning. These materially extend the factual-editing and downstream-capability coverage retained from v1; CKnowEdit is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds InstructEdit for all three original models. New Table 2 evaluates SERAC, GRACE and MELO against AlphaEdit on Counterfact and ZsRE, extending comparisons to memory-based editing. These methods were only discussed as related work in v1; the original evaluated comparators remain.

E3.justification: The original 2,000-example, 100-edits-per-batch comparison remains. Added protocols include Gemma and phi-1.5 backbones, norm-based filtering for KnowEdit, multi-hop evaluation with and without chain-of-thought, long-form consistency metrics, and a sweep over 10–100% of the data used to estimate K0.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.8 directly tests dependence on the data used to estimate preserved knowledge, revealing greater sensitivity in specificity than in efficacy or generalization. Appendix C.9 adds a runtime comparison testing the overhead claim. Existing case studies, reduced-batch tests, representation analyses and semantic-category comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: V3 explicitly identifies Table 4's uncertainty terms as standard deviations. Conversely, Figure 5's caption no longer identifies its retained dashed contours as 0.95 confidence intervals. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds; the additional tables alone do not establish a changed repetition procedure.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive results for new comparators, models, tasks, data-size settings and runtime. Table 5 reports GPT-J multi-hop/CoT scores of 5.03/9.14; Table 6 reports LLaMA3 Counterfact specificity of 67.88 with full K0 data versus 56.12 with 10%. Existing Table 1 means remain, but ROME's LLaMA3 efficacy uncertainty changes from 0.47 to 0.41. Section 4.3 removes the explicit 98.48% capability-retention summary.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the formal statement from B being in the null space of B to B being in the null space of A when BA = 0. The substantive objectives, derivations and proofs in Appendices B.2–B.4 remain unchanged; introducing a separate symbol for the projected perturbation is only clarification.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion change the claimed average performance improvement from 36.4% to 36.7%, matching the figure already stated in v1's introduction. The central claims about null-space preservation and a one-line enhancement to existing editing methods retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations linking memory-based methods' preservation advantages to storage, instability to large hidden-state norms, and specificity to K0 data coverage. Its main-text limitations section replaces v1's Appendix D: the small-edit advantage caveat and untested-paradigm discussion disappear, while unexplored multimodal and reasoning-model applicability becomes the focus.

D1.justification: The original layer selections, optimization settings, A40 hardware and code-access statement remain. V1's per-sample timing statements are removed and v3 provides dataset/model-specific timings per 100 edits in Table 7. The filtering mechanism is newly documented, but its threshold and excluded-sample counts are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 5 replaces the projection-based continual-learning discussion covering OWM, OGD, Orthog-Subspace, GPM and TRGP with a benchmark-evaluation discussion. It also adds InstructEdit and AnyEdit coverage and expands the discussion of WISE. This substantially changes research positioning, although the foundational Adam-NSCL citation remains.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized wording and explanatory edits, updates author and publication information, reorganizes related work, and moves rewritten limitations into the main text. Appendix C gains dedicated subsections for additional experiments. Much of the original introduction, method, research-question structure and analysis prose remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 expands Table 1, adds six tables and a data-size sensitivity figure, and redraws Figure 3 with the same conceptual content. Figure 7 moves and gains axis explanations. Most original experimental graphics and dataset examples retain identical artwork, despite relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The K0-size study tests a central preservation dependency left unexamined in v1, while broader comparator/task coverage and measured runtime strengthen empirical validation. These benefits are tempered by unspecified filtering thresholds and exclusion counts, multi-hop claims in Appendix C.7 that contradict Table 5, and removal of the earlier small-edit limitation. The revision provides useful additional evidence, but reporting and qualification problems limit the net quality gain.
